prompt:
I need the front end for Holdfast Reception. An AI phone receptionist for one-person trade businesses that answers calls while the owner is on a job, and that the owner sets up with their own hours, prices, service area and rules about what it may say or book.

Who's using it: Rafael 'Rafa' Domínguez, a licensed locksmith who runs Domínguez Lock & Key alone out of a van in suburban Phoenix. He's good with phones and tools but not with software settings; he signed up three weeks ago and has been listening to the call recordings at night.

What they're doing right now: Rafa just listened to a recording where the assistant quoted a caller $65 for a car lockout at 11 p.m. when his after-hours rate is $125, and in another it told someone he services Apache Junction, which he stopped doing. Tonight he wants to fix how it behaves: correct the after-hours pricing, shrink the service area, make it stop booking safe-opening jobs and instead take a message, and change how it talks. Callers said it sounded too formal, and he wants it to say upfront that it's his assistant and not him. He also wants it to text him immediately for anyone who says a child or pet is locked in a car.

What's in the system at this point: Business profile: name, license # ROC 334190, base ZIP 85283, current service area 9 cities (to become 7). Hours: Mon–Sat 7:00–19:00 regular, after-hours 19:00–7:00 and Sundays. Price sheet: 14 services (e.g., residential lockout $85 / after-hours $125; car lockout $65 / $125; rekey per cylinder $25; safe opening 'quote only'). Assistant settings: greeting script, voice (3 options), formality level, disclosure line, languages (English, Spanish), booking rules per service (book / take message / refuse), escalation triggers (keyword phrases like 'baby in car', 'dog in car' → immediate text to (480) 555-0142), max booking window (2 hours ahead). Last 30 days: 212 calls handled, 61 jobs booked, 9 calls flagged by Rafa as 'wrong info'. Sample transcripts available for testing changes against.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
